Matter on the LAW AND MOTION / DISCOVERY CALENDAR for Friday, AUG-07-2026. LINE 7.

PLAINTIFF JOHN MCGLYNN's Motion For Order Clarifying Payment For Arbitration Costs Necessary To Implement Order Compelling Arbitration And Request For Order Specifying San Francisco As Location Of Artbitration.

Plaintiff John McGlynn's motion for order clarifying payment for arbitration costs is granted in part and denied in part. The motion is set for further hearing on September 22, 2026.

***THE COURT'S COMPLETE RULING HAS BEEN EMAILED TO THE PARTIES***

For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 301 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 301 Zoom ID 161 502 4290; Passcode 700956.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number.

Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept301tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept301tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested.

The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion or Discovery Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(301/CVA)

MINI MINUTES: PLAINTIFF JOHN MCGLYNN's Motion For Order Clarifying Payment For Arbitration Costs Necessary To Implement Order Compelling Arbitration And Request For Order Specifying San Francisco As Location Of Artbitration.

Appearances (in court):
John McGlynn, in propria persona, Petitioner.
No other appearances.

Not contested/argued. The court reminds Petitioner re: the timely submission of intent to appear to argue. The court adopts its tentative ruling as follows: Plaintiff John McGlynn's motion for order clarifying payment for arbitration costs is granted in part and denied in part. The motion is set for further hearing on September 22, 2026.

To the extent the motion seeks reconsideration of the court's prior order compelling arbitration and staying judicial proceedings, it is jurisdictionally barred because it is not brought within 10 days of the prior ruling and does not state new evidence or law that could not have been presented on the prior motion. (Code Civ. Proc., sec. 1008.)

To the extent the motion seeks relief from the arbitration stay for an order requiring Extra Space Storage to pay some or all of the arbitration fees that McGlynn anticipates with his chosen provider, AAA, the motion is granted in part. Under Aronow v. Superior Court (2022) 76 Cal.App.5th 865, this court has the authority to lift the arbitration stay and conduct an evidentiary hearing about McGlynn's ability to pay arbitration fees and the likely cost of arbitration. The court sets this further hearing for September 22, 2026. McGlynn may submit a brief discussing the Aronow factors and all evidence in support of his request by August 24, 2026, including his estimate of the cost of arbitration. He may conditionally lodge under seal any confidential financial information and file a motion to seal pursuant to Rule of Court 2.550. McGlynn's moving papers here provide his income and expenses but no information about assets. Extra Space may file an opposition brief by September 8, 2026. The opposition brief should contain Extra Space's estimate of the cost of arbitration with AAA or other providers capable of administering this arbitration if Extra Space disagrees with McGlynn's estimate. Aronow discusses the possibility of financial discovery; if Extra Space seeks a continuance for financial discovery it should make that request in its opposition papers. McGlynn may file a reply brief by September 15, 2026.

The court is aware from its experience with major arbitration providers' rules that some arbitration providers, including AAA, require businesses to pay the cost of arbitration other than a filing fee in a consumer arbitration matter. The parties shall address in their briefs the effect, if any, of these rules on McGlynn's motion, and whether AAA will require Extra Space to pay for the arbitration under its consumer arbitration rules as a condition of administering the arbitration even if the contract requires McGlynn to pay all costs above $2500.

McGlynn shall follow Rule of Court 2.108 about line spacing, and other rules of court concerning formatting and font size, when he files future briefs.

The prevailing party is required to prepare and submit to Dept. 301 a proposed form of order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling.

Judge: Christine Van Aken. Clerk: Robert Woods. Not Reported. (301/CVA)
